correctness.rationale: The exact Faulhaber polynomial and its odd symmetry determine all seven residue branches. Four have unit derivatives and are isometric onto three whole balls. The centered class at -1/2 maps via an explicit unit-slope polynomial bijectively onto 49Z_7. Unique simple critical points above residues 1 and 5 give analytic quadratic normal forms with isometric coordinates, hence two separated translated-square images. Their root counts yield every prime-power fiber, Q(m), V(k), 25/56 Haar measure, and exact least period 7^k. The packaged checker passed 274512 complete target and recurrence comparisons for k<=6, corroborating but not replacing the all-k proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is an explicit image-and-fiber classification of the degree-five fourth-power Faulhaber map at seven, including an image-redundant central branch with ninefold fibers. The inspected sources give general residue-ring bounds, finite-field value-set bounds, general monomial lifting, or classifications of distinct polynomials and different sumset quantifiers. None of their inspected statements yields this exact output without a new branch calculation. The full text of a relevant general 1995 article was inaccessible, leaving a historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: For the classical integer sequence of consecutive fourth-power sums, seven is the first prime larger than all primes dividing the Faulhaber denominator 30. Its derivative unexpectedly has a double reduced critical root at 3 as well as two simple roots, producing a redundant 49Z_7 branch with exact ninefold fibers while two other branches contribute distinct square sheets. The all-depth image and fiber law, least period and exact Haar measure 25/56 answer a motivated local representability problem; it is not an arbitrary isolated residue or tabular recomputation. The claim does not assert a general or downstream theorem.
